## Deviations (recorded, not smoothed)

1. **`joined-boundary` needed a second detector.** The first draft
   flagged only a word character flush against an inline tag — the
   planted `concern?<a` fixture (K14 NEW-7's verbatim class) slipped
   because `?` is not a word character. The detector now covers
   sentence punctuation (`.?!,;:…`) before an inline tag AND two
   inline elements abutting (`</span><span` — P36.23's own recorded
   fix-arc-2 class), while `(`, quotes and dashes stay legitimate
   openings.
2. **The readability mean counts the footer too.** The first fixture
   (one 30-word sentence) read under the 22-word threshold because
   the footer's 8-word stamp diluted the mean to 19 — faithful to
   "the page", kept; the fixture grew to three long sentences so the
   advisory leg exercises honestly.
3. **No ADR, no copy-batch rows.** Every shape executes
   already-answered decision lines (K14 UXK14-5's own list,
   DR-K14-10/11/19 verbatim, DR-C6-28, CP-4/CP-8, K13 §7 W1, the
   `data-sig-count="dedup"` interval contract SIG-UI-063 names).
   The lint ships no reader-facing sentences, so no `CK-*` rows
   exist to pin — the publish-gate path is untouched.
4. **`data-technical-details` / `data-identifiers` /
   `data-sig-count="dedup"` are forward contracts.** SIG-UI-053
   names Identifiers/Technical-details blocks as the only lawful
   home for UUIDs and registry ids, and SIG-UI-063 names the
   de-duplicated interval; nothing emits those markers today (the
   surfaces that will land them name their own rows). The lint
   defines the exemption shape now so the flip tickets inherit a
   check that already understands them.
5. **The corpus includes internal and T3 routes.** `/component-kit/`
   and `/curate/**` sit in the same manifest; excluding them would
   be a hand-maintained route list — the class the registry exists
   to prevent. Their findings report like every route's.
